name: Intersect (Intersect Power, LLC; Intersect Power Holdings, LLC) — a Google subsidiary since 10 March 2026
headquarters: San Francisco, California (140 New Montgomery Street, announced May 2025); collaboration hubs in San Diego, New York, Denver, Austin, Calgary and Toronto per the company; earlier releases gave Houston (2023) and Oakland (2022)
employees: Not stated by the company. Proxies only: the 2019 portfolio release described 'roughly 20 people'; Forbes' 2025 Best Startup Employers list requires at least 50 employees; the 2025 headquarters release says about a quarter of staff are Bay Area-based. Collection gap.
summary:
BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Intersect is a Google subsidiary — Alphabet announced the acquisition on 22 December 2025 at USD 4.75 billion in cash plus assumed debt, closed it on 10 March 2026, and books it at USD 5,868 million in its Q2 2026 10-Q — but Google bought only the 'digital power' development platform, its team and the Texas energy parks; the grid-tied fleet Intersect had built (about 4.4 GW of solar and 8.8 GWh of storage in construction or operation, per TPG) was carved out at closing into IPX Power under TPG Rise Climate, CAI and Greenbelt, and no source says Intersect develops for anyone but its parent now. The premise 'Google-owned since 2026' is correct on the close date; the premise of a Wyoming campus is unsupported — the named parks are Quantum (Haskell County), Meitner (Gray and Roberts Counties) and Roman (Deaf Smith County), all in Texas.

BACKGROUND. Founded in 2016 by Sheldon Kimber (ex-COO of Recurrent Energy), Intersect developed and sold 1.7 GWdc of solar by 2019, then raised USD 127 million (2021), USD 750 million led by TPG Rise Climate (2022) and 'over $800 million' led by TPG and Google (December 2024) to build and own Athos III, Radian, Oberon and Lumina — 2.2 GWdc of solar and 2.4 GWh of storage financed in USD 2.6 billion (2021), USD 3.075 billion (2022) and USD 837 million (2024) rounds with HPS Investment Partners, MUFG and Santander, on hedges, corporate offtake and merchant batteries rather than utility PPAs. The December 2024 partnership made Google 'anchor tenant' of co-located parks; a year later Google bought the developer. Quantum's 640 MW of solar and 1.3 GWh of storage began operating in June 2026 with the Google data centre under construction; Meitner — 'more than a gigawatt of wind, solar, and battery storage' with 'a minority share' of demand from on-site gas — launched construction on 4 June 2026 after Gray County replaced a hydrogen abatement with a data-centre abatement conditioned on air cooling. Supply is concentrated in First Solar (11.4 GWdc ordered by 2029) and Tesla (15.3 GWh of Megapacks). Kimber, Ross, Rymill, Spicer, Hanson, Bain and Antonopoulos lead the Google-era company; the former CFO, COO and CCO went to IPX.

Collection gaps: data-centre megawatts, gas capacity and contract values at every park (the 840 MW Meitner load figure is New Project Media's reading of filings); any FERC Section 203, ERCOT large-load or PUCT SB 6 record naming an Intersect or Google entity; headcount; the split of the First Solar and Tesla frameworks between Intersect and IPX; and any post-acquisition project financing.
ecosystemRole: Intersect is the clearest case in this corpus of storage attaching to AI load behind one interconnection: a developer that put solar, wind, batteries and gas on the same site as a hyperscaler's data centre, then became part of the hyperscaler. For a supplier or EPC it is now a Google procurement channel with its own engineering, construction and procurement heads; for the utilities and ISOs it is an ERCOT co-located load governed by SB 6; for the sponsors it was a USD 12 billion combined exit.

productsAndServices.name: Co-located energy parks for Google (Quantum, Meitner, Roman)
productsAndServices.category: Development, construction and operation — behind-the-meter campuses
productsAndServices.description: The business Google bought: development, construction and operation of campuses where a Google data centre sits behind one fence with dedicated generation and storage. Named sites, all in Texas, per Intersect's portfolio pages and the June 2026 Google–Intersect release: Quantum (Haskell County — 640 MW of solar and 1.3 GWh of storage across two facilities, generation 'will begin operations this month' in June 2026, the Google data centre 'recently began construction'); Meitner Energy Center (Gray and Roberts Counties — 'a data center co-located with more than a gigawatt of wind, solar, and battery storage systems', 'a minority share of the site's demand met by firming on-site gas', air-cooled, construction launched 4 June 2026); and Roman (Deaf Smith County — 'in development', wind, solar, storage, natural-gas firming and an air-cooled data centre). Intersect describes the model as 'co-locating industrial demand with dedicated gas and renewable power generation'.
highlights: Google is the customer at every named park; Alphabet's acquisition release says the sites are 'multiple gigawatts of energy and data center projects currently in development or under construction' from the December 2024 partnership.

Data-centre megawatts are not published by either party for any site. The only load figure in the record is New Project Media's reading of Meitner filings — 840 MW of behind-the-meter data-centre load in up to three phases, replacing a 400 MW electrolysis plan.

Gray County's abatement (15 October 2025) is conditioned on an air-cooled data centre with a claw-back of abated taxes if cooling changes, and the county abolished the 2024 hydrogen abatement the same day.
Meitner is the first named Intersect project to add on-site gas generation; the 2022–2024 releases described the same site as solar, wind and green hydrogen.
productsAndServices.positioning: Against the other AI-campus developers in this corpus — Crusoe's flare-gas and islanded model, the neocloud landlords' leased shells — Intersect's distinguishing feature is ownership: since March 2026 the developer and the tenant are the same corporate group, so the campus is neither leased nor contracted but built for the parent. Intersect's founder had argued since 2021 that 'long-term offtake contracts actually destroy value' and since 2024 that 'load will come to the location of power generation'.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Built for the parent after 10 March 2026; before that, under a December 2024 partnership in which 'Google will serve as anchor tenant in newly constructed industrial parks' and Greenbelt describes 'a 20-year off-take and powered-land lease' for Quantum.
targetSegments: Google's technical infrastructure organisation (the sole named customer)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Quantum generation operating from June 2026 with the data centre under construction; Meitner Phase 1 'operational late 2028' with wind and solar in service October 2027 per New Project Media's reading of filings; Roman in development with no dates. Alphabet's 2025 release: 10.8 GW of projects expected by 2028 per Reuters; the December 2024 partnership targeted 'USD 20 billion in renewable power infrastructure investment by the end of the decade'.

productsAndServices.name: Grid-tied solar and storage fleet (developed by Intersect; owned by IPX Power since March 2026)
productsAndServices.category: Development track record — carved out at the sale
productsAndServices.description: The projects Intersect developed, financed and operated as an independent power producer before the sale, which Alphabet's release says 'will remain independent, backed by existing investors TPG Rise Climate, Climate Adaptive Infrastructure, and Greenbelt Capital Partners' and which launched as IPX Power on 10 March 2026 with 'approximately 4.4 GW of solar PV and 8.8 GWh of battery storage in construction or operation'. Per Intersect's own COD releases: Athos III (Riverside County, 310 MWp / 224 MWac plus 448 MWh, COD 22 December 2022), Radian (Brown County TX, 415 MWp / 320 MWac, COD 16 May 2023, Merrill Lynch Commodities hedge), Oberon I and II (Riverside County, 679 MWp / 500 MWac plus 250 MW / 1 GWh, COD November 2023, offtake to Calpine Energy Solutions, Constellation, Ava Community Energy, Microsoft and San Diego Community Power), Lumina I and II (Scurry County TX, 828 MWp / 640 MWac, COD 3 January 2024, RECs to 'two Fortune 100 companies') and three 160 MW / 320 MWh standalone Texas batteries (Lumina I, Lumina II, Radian BESS — 86 Tesla Megapacks each, Autobidder on two, operational 2024). Darden (Fresno County, 1.15 GWac / 4.6 GWh, COD 2028) went to IPX with the fleet.
highlights: Every project used First Solar modules and, where storage was included, Tesla Megapacks; Intersect's about page states '17.7 GWh of Tesla Megapacks secured' and 'a multi-billion dollar commitment with First Solar'.

The fleet was financed in three portfolio rounds — USD 2.6 billion (November 2021), USD 3.075 billion (September 2022) and USD 837 million for the Texas batteries (July 2024) — with HPS Investment Partners as term lender throughout and MUFG and Santander as construction leads.
TPG's closing release puts the combined enterprise value of the Google sale and the IPX spin-out at USD 12 billion; Greenbelt's page lists IPX at seven projects with Darden the largest.
The 1.7 GWdc of projects Intersect developed and sold before 2021 (Juno, Titan, Aragorn, Athos I and II) is the develop-to-sell chapter; the 2021–2024 fleet is develop-to-own.
productsAndServices.positioning: This is the record that made the platform saleable: a developer that took 2.2 GWdc of solar and 2.4 GWh of storage from financing to COD in three years, largely on hedges and merchant batteries rather than utility PPAs. Since March 2026 it belongs to IPX Power and is described here as Intersect's history, not its holdings.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Held in project companies under Intersect Power Holdings until the carve-out; power sold through hedges (Radian), CCA and corporate offtake (Oberon), RECs (Lumina) and merchant dispatch with Tesla Autobidder (Texas batteries).
targetSegments: Community-choice aggregators and retailers (Ava, San Diego Community Power, Calpine Energy Solutions)
Corporate buyers (Microsoft, Constellation, two unnamed Fortune 100 companies)
productsAndServices.roadmap: None for Intersect — the fleet and its pipeline are IPX Power's. IPX closed USD 4.95 billion for Darden (May 2026) and an USD 800 million corporate facility (August 2026).

productsAndServices.name: Power-first siting and the hybrid generation stack
productsAndServices.description: Intersect's stated method: site the load where large, cheap generation can be built rather than where transmission already exists ('the grid is broken'; 'load will come to the location of power generation'), and serve it with 'extremely cheap solar and wind' for '50–70% of the hours in a year', batteries, and 'peaking gas generation' with 'lower up front capital cost than combined cycle gas turbine (CCGT) baseload' — the founder's 2025 phrase is 'not your grandparents' baseload power'. The founder claimed in September 2024 that Intersect 'has fully developed single projects capable of hosting loads as large as 3GW+'. Its FERC filing, quoted by Utility Dive, complained that 'the lack of standard rules, practices and procedures for integrating co-located [load] with new and existing generation means co-location configurations must go through a laborious, unpredictable semi-discretionary process to interconnect'.
highlights: Meitner's county record shows the method in practice: a 2023 presentation of 340 MW solar plus 460 MW wind with 400 MW of electrolysis became, by mid-2025 filings, 840 MW of behind-the-meter data-centre load with amended interconnection agreements with Cross Texas Transmission.
The Gray County presentation stated 'most of the power produced by the project will be used onsite, reducing reliance on the transmission grid', with grid export 'when the system needs power'.

No FERC surplus-interconnection request, ERCOT large-load queue entry, PUCT Project 55999 filing or private-use-network registration naming an Intersect entity was found — the structures are described in county records and press, not in a regulator's docket. Collection gap.
Intersect's about page lists a Head of Microgrids among fifteen department heads, and its site claims '11.5+ GW of clean energy capacity across 14 facilities'.
productsAndServices.positioning: The claim Intersect sells to its parent is speed: Alphabet's June 2026 investor presentation says the acquisition 'will help us come to market even faster', and Sundar Pichai's release quote is 'operate more nimbly in building new power generation in lockstep with new data center load'.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Internal to Google after the sale.
targetSegments: Google data-centre siting in ERCOT (Haskell, Gray, Roberts and Deaf Smith Counties)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Google's data-centre location pages list Pampa, Texas 'in development' and new campuses in Armstrong, Haskell, Pampa and Wilbarger Counties; only Haskell and Pampa are tied to Intersect in any source.

productsAndServices.name: Procurement programme — First Solar modules and Tesla Megapacks
productsAndServices.description: Multi-year framework orders that pre-date the sale and now sit partly with IPX Power and partly with Google-owned Intersect (the split is not published): First Solar — 1.7 GW of Series 6 (September 2019), 2.4 GWdc for 2024–2026 delivery (July 2022) and 4.9 GWdc of Series 6 Plus and Series 7 for 2025–2029 (November 2022), which Intersect said took its 2022 orders to 7.3 GWdc and its cumulative First Solar procurement to 11.4 GWdc by 2029; Tesla — 15.3 GWh of Megapacks announced 18 July 2024, 'more than half' for four California and Texas projects by end-2027 and the rest for 2028–2030 from the Lathrop Megafactory, with the about page now citing 17.7 GWh secured.
highlights: Intersect framed the First Solar orders as domestic-content positioning: Athos III used 'American-made components to meet IRA domestic content requirements' and Oberon used Ohio-made modules, Lathrop-made Megapacks and American steel with union labour.
The founder's 2024 blog said battery cells were 'mostly' from China and expected that to shift under policy pressure — the one FEOC-adjacent statement in the record.
EPCs on the operating fleet were Signal Energy (2019–2023 projects); no EPC, integrator or gas-turbine supplier is named for Quantum, Meitner or Roman.
productsAndServices.positioning: Two-vendor concentration by design — one module maker, one battery integrator — which is the opposite of the dual-sourcing pattern this corpus's Plus Power dossier describes.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Tesla deliveries 2028–2030 under the 2024 order; First Solar deliveries to 2029.

productsAndServices.name: Corporate capital formation (2020–2026)
productsAndServices.description: Equity per Intersect's own releases: USD 127 million from Climate Adaptive Infrastructure and Trilantic North America (January 2021, with a USD 482 million Generate Capital and CarVal debt facility); USD 750 million led by TPG Rise Climate with CAI and Trilantic Energy Partners North America (June 2022); 'over USD 800 million' led by TPG Rise Climate and Google with CAI and Greenbelt Capital Partners (10 December 2024 — Greenbelt's page splits it as USD 879 million, USD 250 million from Google, unconfirmed by Google); 'over USD 2.1 billion in corporate equity raised' cumulative (October 2025). Corporate debt: an up-to-USD 800 million revolving credit facility (June 2023; Deutsche Bank, Nomura, Santander CIB). Then the sale: USD 4.75 billion in cash plus assumed debt (Alphabet, 22 December 2025), USD 4.8 billion in Alphabet's 10-K, USD 5.9 billion 'after purchase price adjustments' with USD 1,214 million of debt assumed in Alphabet's Q1 2026 10-Q (final allocation USD 5,868 million in the Q2 10-Q).
highlights: Alphabet consolidates Intersect as a variable-interest entity with goodwill of USD 2,174 million and property and equipment of USD 5,129 million, allocated across Google Services and Google Cloud.

TPG 'initially invested in Intersect in 2022' and sold its stake at closing while taking majority ownership of IPX Power; Greenbelt dates its own investment to December 2020 and calls the position 'realized'.

The founder said in December 2023 that Intersect had raised USD 1.3 billion of equity and USD 5–6 billion of project finance and expected about USD 200 million of EBITDA to triple by early 2027 — a podcast statement, not a filing.
productsAndServices.positioning: The one private developer in this corpus whose exit is priced in an acquirer's 10-Q rather than a press report.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Growth-equity rounds, then a strategic sale.
targetSegments: Climate-infrastructure growth funds (TPG Rise Climate, CAI, Greenbelt)
productsAndServices.roadmap: None — the company is now funded by its parent; no Google-era project financing for Quantum or Meitner was found.

recentDevelopments.headline: IPX Power — the carved-out grid-tied fleet, not Intersect — closes an USD 800 million corporate facility (USD 600 million revolver, USD 200 million LC)
recentDevelopments.read: The former Intersect fleet now finances itself independently; nothing comparable has been published for the Google-owned entity.

recentDevelopments.headline: Alphabet's Q2 2026 10-Q records the final Intersect purchase-price allocation: total USD 5,868 million, goodwill USD 2,174 million, property and equipment USD 5,129 million, debt assumed USD 1,214 million
recentDevelopments.read: The only audited valuation of a private developer in this corpus — and USD 1.1 billion above the USD 4.75 billion headline once adjustments and assumed debt are counted.

recentDevelopments.headline: Google and Intersect launch construction of the Meitner Energy Center (Gray and Roberts Counties): a data centre co-located with more than a gigawatt of wind, solar and storage plus on-site gas firming; Quantum's 640 MW / 1.3 GWh generation 'will begin operations this month'
recentDevelopments.read: The first post-acquisition project adds gas to a model that was sold as solar-plus-storage; the data-centre megawatts are still unpublished.

recentDevelopments.headline: Alphabet's investor presentation: 'Our recent acquisition of Intersect will help us come to market even faster'
recentDevelopments.read: The parent frames the purchase as time-to-power, not as an energy business.

recentDevelopments.headline: IPX Power closes USD 4.95 billion of debt for Darden (Fresno County, 1.15 GWac solar and 4.6 GWh of storage, COD 2028), including USD 2.13 billion of ITC purchase agreements
recentDevelopments.read: The largest financing in the record belongs to the fleet Google chose not to buy.

recentDevelopments.headline: Alphabet's Q1 2026 10-Q: acquisition completed 10 March 2026 'for $5.9 billion, after purchase price adjustments'; Intersect consolidated as a variable-interest entity with goodwill allocated to Google Services and Google Cloud
recentDevelopments.read: Consolidation into the cloud and services segments tells a supplier which Google budget the campuses sit in.

recentDevelopments.headline: PUCT adopts SB 6 net-metering rules for co-located data centres of 75 MW or more; the Crusoe–Google campus at Goodnight is the first test case
recentDevelopments.read: The rule that governs every Intersect park was written after the deal was signed; Intersect has not appeared in the docket.

recentDevelopments.headline: Energy-Storage.news reports the acquisition complete, Google having acquired TPG Rise Climate's share; the grid-tied business separated into IPX Power
recentDevelopments.read: Trade press confirmation of the sellers' 10 March releases.

recentDevelopments.headline: TPG and Greenbelt announce completion of the USD 4.75 billion (plus debt) sale of Intersect to Google and the launch of IPX Power — about 4.4 GW of solar and 8.8 GWh of storage in construction or operation, TPG Rise Climate majority, CAI and Greenbelt; 'a combined enterprise value of $12 billion'
recentDevelopments.read: Google bought the developer and the parks; the investors kept the fleet and the CFO, COO and CCO who ran it.

recentDevelopments.headline: Alphabet's FY2025 10-K: agreement to acquire Intersect 'for $4.8 billion in cash, plus the assumption of debt', closing expected in the first half of 2026
recentDevelopments.read: The 10-K rounds the headline up; the 10-Qs later move it to USD 5.9 billion.

recentDevelopments.headline: Utility Dive: Alphabet takes about 3.6 GW of Texas solar and wind and 3.1 GWh of storage in development; the investor group keeps the operating assets plus a 1.6 GW / 4.8 GWh California project; 10.8 GW expected by late 2028
recentDevelopments.read: The perimeter of the deal, as trade press reconstructed it — no party has published a project-by-project split.

recentDevelopments.headline: Alphabet announces a definitive agreement to acquire Intersect for USD 4.75 billion in cash plus debt assumption; Kimber stays as CEO under the Intersect brand; Texas operating assets and California properties excluded
recentDevelopments.read: A hyperscaler buys a developer rather than signing PPAs: the premise 'Google-owned since 2026' is confirmed, with the announcement in 2025 and the close in March 2026.

recentDevelopments.headline: Kimber's blog 'It Goes to 11': Intersect 'will remain Intersect, remaining separate from Alphabet and Google under the Intersect brand'; a portion of assets to be divested to existing investors who will 'continue to construct billions of dollars in new assets, including the world's largest BESS'
recentDevelopments.read: The founder's own account of the split, written before the IPX name existed.

recentDevelopments.headline: Google announces a USD 40 billion Texas investment through 2027, including a Haskell County data centre 'built alongside a new solar and battery storage plant'
recentDevelopments.read: Google named the county but not the developer; Intersect's Quantum is the plant.

recentDevelopments.headline: Katrina Rymill (ex-Equinix SVP Corporate Finance and Sustainability) appointed CFO; the release states USD 15 billion of assets in operation or under construction and 'over $2.1 billion in corporate equity raised'
recentDevelopments.read: A data-centre-industry CFO hired seven weeks before the Google agreement.

recentDevelopments.headline: Gray County's judge says the Meitner data-centre abatement was approved for a 'high profile tenant' he 'could not share … just yet'
recentDevelopments.read: The tenant was Google; the county record preceded the deal announcement by eight weeks.

recentDevelopments.headline: Gray County approves the Meitner data-centre abatement and a road-use agreement and abolishes the 2024 hydrogen abatement; the abatement is conditioned on an air-cooled data centre with a claw-back
recentDevelopments.read: The county wrote the cooling technology into the tax deal.

recentDevelopments.headline: Intersect's letter to Gray County neighbours: it 'is planning to develop an air-cooled data center instead of a hydrogen facility'; commissioners grant a 30-day extension on abatement talks
recentDevelopments.read: The public record of the hydrogen-to-data-centre pivot, five months before Google announced the acquisition.

recentDevelopments.headline: Texas SB 6 signed: loads of 75 MW or more must accept curtailment in firm load shed and install shutoff equipment; PUCT to review co-location net-metering
recentDevelopments.read: The statute that now governs every Intersect campus.

recentDevelopments.headline: California Energy Commission issues its final order certifying Darden (1,150 MW PV, 4,600 MWh) under the AB 205 opt-in process, the 800 MW hydrogen facility removed
recentDevelopments.read: The second hydrogen retreat in the record; the project went to IPX at the carve-out.

recentDevelopments.headline: Energy Risk names the USD 837 million Texas battery financing Deal of the Year; Kimber: about USD 4 billion of assets managed, USD 9 billion breaking ground in 2025 and a similar amount in 2026, and Intersect 'prepared to build a more merchant fleet, managing it using our trading team'

relationships.scale: USD 4.75 billion in cash plus assumed debt (announced); USD 5,868 million total purchase price (Alphabet Q2 2026 10-Q)
relationships.via: Alphabet acquisition; Quantum and Meitner energy parks
relationships.note: Alphabet agreed on 22 December 2025 and closed on 10 March 2026 the acquisition of Intersect, after leading the December 2024 round as a minority holder; Google is the data-centre customer at Quantum (Haskell County) and Meitner (Gray and Roberts Counties).
relationships.context: The relationship ran in three stages. In December 2024 Google and TPG Rise Climate led an 'over $800 million' round and Google agreed to 'serve as anchor tenant in newly constructed industrial parks' — Greenbelt describes 'a 20-year off-take and powered-land lease' for Quantum. In December 2025 Alphabet announced the acquisition of 'Intersect's team and multiple gigawatts of energy and data center projects currently in development or under construction' for USD 4.75 billion plus debt, excluding the Texas operating assets and California properties. On 10 March 2026 the deal closed; Alphabet's 10-Qs consolidate Intersect as a variable-interest entity at USD 5.9 billion with goodwill allocated to Google Services and Google Cloud, and the June 2026 investor presentation says the purchase 'will help us come to market even faster'. Sundar Pichai's stated rationale: 'operate more nimbly in building new power generation in lockstep with new data center load'.

relationships.scale: 15.3 GWh Megapack order (July 2024); '17.7 GWh of Tesla Megapacks secured' (about page); 258 Megapacks across three Texas batteries
relationships.note: Tesla agreed in July 2024 to supply 15.3 GWh of Megapacks for Intersect's solar-plus-storage projects; Megapacks were installed at Athos III, Oberon and the three Texas standalone batteries, two of which run on Tesla's Autobidder.
relationships.context: Intersect's 18 July 2024 release, with Tesla Energy's Mike Snyder quoted, put 'more than half' of the 15.3 GWh into four California and Texas projects by end-2027 and the balance into 2028–2030 deliveries from the Lathrop Megafactory. The three 160 MW / 320 MWh Texas batteries financed the same week used 86 Megapacks each; Oberon's COD release credited Lathrop-built Megapacks. Simon Ross, Intersect's CCO, was previously Tesla's deputy general counsel for the energy business. The order pre-dates the March 2026 carve-out, and neither party has said how it is split between Google-owned Intersect and IPX Power.

relationships.scale: share of Oberon's 679 MWp / 1 GWh output (not broken out)
relationships.note: Intersect's Oberon COD release names Microsoft among the project's offtakers with Calpine Energy Solutions, Constellation, Ava Community Energy and San Diego Community Power.
relationships.context: Oberon (Riverside County, 679 MWp solar plus 250 MW / 1 GWh storage) reached commercial operation on 14 November 2023 selling energy, RECs and resource adequacy to a group of buyers that included Microsoft; the release does not size any buyer's share. The asset passed to IPX Power at the March 2026 carve-out, so the contract is now IPX's rather than Intersect's — hence historical for this dossier. Microsoft appears nowhere as a tenant of an Intersect energy park.

relationships.scale: share of Oberon's output (not broken out)
relationships.note: 'Constellation' is named among Oberon's offtakers in Intersect's 14 November 2023 COD release and in Ava Community Energy's account of the same milestone.
relationships.context: Constellation took a share of Oberon's energy, RECs and resource adequacy alongside Calpine Energy Solutions, Ava, Microsoft and San Diego Community Power; the contract size is not published. As with Microsoft, the asset moved to IPX Power in March 2026, and no Constellation link to the Google-era parks exists in the record.

relationships.note: Intersect's CFO Katrina Rymill joined from Equinix, where she was SVP Corporate Finance and Sustainability, in October 2025.
relationships.context: The hire is the one documented link between Intersect and the colocation industry's largest operator: Rymill ran global treasury, investor relations and sustainability at Equinix and raised USD 9 billion of green bonds there, per Intersect's appointment release. No commercial relationship between the companies is stated in any source.

relationships.note: Latitude Media describes the Crusoe–Google campus at Goodnight as Texas's first SB 6 co-location net-metering test case under the rules the PUCT adopted in March 2026 — the same regime Intersect's Google parks operate under.
relationships.context: Crusoe and Intersect are the two developers in this corpus building behind-the-meter campuses for Google in ERCOT. Latitude Media's April 2026 report on the Goodnight case explains the PUCT's 60-day review of net-metering arrangements for merchant generators registered before 1 September 2025 that co-locate with new load, and notes ERCOT has required transmission studies for co-location since 2022. Intersect does not appear in the docket; the link is the shared customer and the shared rule, not a stated commercial tie.

policyExposure.exposure: Every named Intersect campus is an ERCOT co-located load above 75 MW, the threshold at which SB 6 (signed 20–21 June 2025) requires curtailment during firm load shed, on-site shutoff equipment, a USD 100,000 minimum interconnection fee and PUCT review of net-metering arrangements between merchant generators and new co-located load; the PUCT adopted its net-metering rules for co-located data centres in late March 2026. Baker Botts notes an exemption where the same parent held majority ownership of both generator and load on 1 January 2025 — a date before Google owned Intersect. No SB 6, PUCT Project 55999 or ERCOT large-load filing naming an Intersect or Google entity was found. Collection gap.

Intersect told FERC, per Utility Dive, that 'the lack of standard rules, practices and procedures for integrating co-located [load] with new and existing generation means co-location configurations must go through a laborious, unpredictable semi-discretionary process to interconnect'. No surplus-interconnection service request, Order 845 filing or FERC Section 203 record for the Alphabet transaction was found; Texas campuses interconnect under ERCOT's non-FERC regime through Cross Texas Transmission (Meitner, per New Project Media).

policyExposure.regime: Texas Chapter 312 abatements and county reinvestment zones
policyExposure.exposure: Gray County approved a data-centre abatement for IP Meitner in the Meitner Reinvestment Zone on 15 October 2025 — 100 per cent property-tax abatement for ten years per phase according to New Project Media's reading of the filings — and abolished the January 2024 hydrogen abatement; the county conditioned the abatement on an air-cooled data centre with back taxes due if cooling changes, and earlier tied the solar and hydrogen abatements to Ogallala groundwater limits and investment in Pampa's wastewater plant. The Google–Intersect release commits that the buildout 'does not pass the costs of its infrastructure growth onto local families' and that Google 'pays for 100% of the power it uses'.
policyExposure.mitigation: Air-cooled design and a USD 10 million Google Texas Water Impact Fund (per the June 2026 release)

policyExposure.regime: ITC/45X — domestic content and storage ITC
policyExposure.exposure: Athos III used 'American-made components to meet IRA domestic content requirements' and Oberon used Ohio-made First Solar modules, Lathrop-made Megapacks and American steel with union labour, per Intersect's COD releases; the USD 837 million Texas battery financing said the projects 'qualify for Investment Tax Credits under the Inflation Reduction Act'. All of those assets are now IPX Power's; IPX's Darden financing uses USD 2.13 billion of ITC purchase agreements. Whether the Google-era parks claim credits, and under which FEOC rules, is not stated by either party.

The founder's May 2024 blog said battery cells were 'mostly' from China and expected that to shift under policy pressure; Intersect's disclosed battery supplier is Tesla (Lathrop) and its module supplier First Solar (Ohio). No Intersect-specific FEOC or tariff statement, and no supplier for Meitner's on-site gas generation, appears in any source read. Collection gap.

policyExposure.regime: California CEQA / AB 205 opt-in certification and BLM DRECP
policyExposure.exposure: Darden (IP Darden I, LLC) was certified by the California Energy Commission on 13 June 2025 under the AB 205 opt-in process with its 800 MW hydrogen facility removed; Aramis survived a CEQA and Measure D petition (denied May 2022, appeal rejected August 2023); Oberon was 'the first project to achieve operation under BLM's Desert Renewable Energy Conservation Plan'. All three are IPX Power assets since March 2026.

periods.commentary: The only audited numbers are the acquirer's purchase-price allocation. Because the grid-tied fleet left with IPX Power at closing, the USD 5.9 billion bought a development platform, a team, three named Texas parks and USD 1.2 billion of debt.

metrics.actual: USD 127 million (CAI, Trilantic — January 2021); USD 750 million (TPG Rise Climate, CAI, Trilantic — June 2022); 'over USD 800 million' (TPG Rise Climate, Google, CAI, Greenbelt — December 2024); 'over USD 2.1 billion' cumulative (company, October 2025)

metrics.name: Project and corporate debt
metrics.actual: USD 482 million corporate facility (Generate Capital, CarVal — 2021); USD 2.6 billion portfolio financing (2021); USD 3.075 billion (2022); up to USD 800 million revolving credit facility (2023); USD 837 million Texas BESS financing (2024)

periods.commentary: Every figure is a release; no consensus or guidance exists, so 'expected' is empty throughout. The founder's stated USD 1.3 billion of equity and USD 5–6 billion of project finance (December 2023) sit between the release totals and are carried as his statement.

financials.commentary: The financial record of Intersect is a capital-formation record that ends in a strategic sale: three growth rounds, three portfolio financings and a revolver, then a purchase price that Alphabet's 10-Q states to the million. What is not in the record is any operating result for the Google-owned entity, any project financing for the Texas parks since closing, or the split of the First Solar and Tesla frameworks between Intersect and IPX.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that Google owns Intersect outright and that the acquisition is closed, not pending. Basis: Alphabet's 22 December 2025 release and FY2025 10-K, TPG's and Greenbelt's 10 March 2026 completion releases, and Alphabet's Q1 and Q2 2026 10-Qs, which consolidate Intersect as a variable-interest entity at USD 5.9 billion. The brief's 'Google-owned since 2026' is confirmed with a March 2026 close; the announcement was December 2025.

(High confidence) We assess that Google bought a development capability and three Texas parks, not an operating power fleet. Basis: Alphabet's release excludes 'Intersect's current Texas operating assets and California properties'; TPG and Greenbelt describe the carve-out of about 4.4 GW of solar and 8.8 GWh of storage into IPX Power with the former CFO, COO and CCO; Alphabet's allocation puts USD 2.2 billion of the USD 5.9 billion into goodwill. The fleet Intersect is known for — Oberon, Lumina, Radian, the Texas batteries, Darden — is now IPX's.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that Intersect is now a captive developer with no third-party customers, and that this was the purpose of the deal. Basis: every named park has Google as tenant; Alphabet's stated rationale is to 'operate more nimbly in building new power generation in lockstep with new data center load'; the June 2026 investor presentation frames the purchase as coming 'to market even faster'; no source says Intersect develops for others after closing. Kimber's blog says Intersect will 'remain separate … under the Intersect brand', which describes governance, not customers.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the energy-park model has moved from 'solar plus storage plus hydrogen' to 'solar, wind and storage firmed by on-site gas', and that this is a design change forced by load, not a rhetorical one. Basis: Meitner's 2023 county presentation (340 MW solar, 460 MW wind, 400 MW electrolysis) became 840 MW of behind-the-meter data-centre load with 'firming on-site gas' by June 2026; Darden's 800 MW hydrogen facility was removed in October 2024; Kimber's April 2025 blog argues for peaking gas at lower capital cost than combined cycle. Gas capacity and its supplier are unpublished.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the binding regulatory exposure is Texas SB 6 and county tax conditions rather than FERC. Basis: every park is an ERCOT co-located load above 75 MW; the PUCT adopted its co-location net-metering rules in March 2026 with a Crusoe–Google campus as the test case; Gray County's abatement carries an air-cooling claw-back; Intersect's own FERC filing complained about co-location process, but no FERC docket naming Intersect was found and ERCOT is outside FERC's interconnection jurisdiction.

(Low confidence) We assess that the pre-sale First Solar and Tesla frameworks are now split between Intersect and IPX Power, with the larger share of near-term Megapack deliveries at IPX's Darden. Basis: the 15.3 GWh Tesla order's 'four California and Texas projects by end-2027' predates the carve-out and Darden is the largest storage project in either company; neither party has published the split. Treat as a question for a supplier's next conversation, not a finding.

Indicators to watch: (1) a data-centre megawatt figure for Quantum or Meitner from Google, Intersect, ERCOT's large-load reports or a PUCT SB 6 filing — the first published load number would size the model; (2) an Intersect entity in a PUCT co-location net-metering review or an ERCOT curtailment filing, which would show which SB 6 path the parks take; (3) any Intersect project with a non-Google tenant, which would refute the captive-developer judgment; (4) a supplier announcement for Meitner's on-site gas (turbines or engines) and any FEOC-compliant battery supply statement — silence past Phase 1 construction would indicate the gas leg is procured through Google; (5) Alphabet's segment disclosures for any Intersect operating result, and IPX Power's next financing naming which Tesla and First Solar volumes it holds.
